close_reason: Added put_crl_if_not_rollback with atomic write-lock across get+compare+put. CrlAtomicPut trait dispatches to atomic path for InMemoryCache, fallback for dyn RevocationCache.
description:
src/cache.rs:659-683: maybe_populate_cache does `self.cache.get_crl(&key)` to check rollback, then `self.cache.put_crl(key, ...)`. Between the two trait calls, another thread can win the race and write a newer entry; this thread then overwrites it with an older fetched CRL.

Trigger: concurrent validation of chains sharing an issuer/CDP-URL, e.g. a TLS server validating many client certs in parallel, or a batch job validating a corpus. Reproducer is simple: two threads each fetch a CRL for the same (issuer_dn, dp_uri); thread A gets CRL with CRLNumber=N, thread B gets CRLNumber=N+1. Both call check_revocation; both run maybe_populate_cache. If thread B's put completes before thread A's get sees it, thread A's get sees no entry (or an older one), is_rollback returns false, and thread A's put writes CRLNumber=N over thread B's N+1.

Bad behavior: defeats the RFC 5280 §5.2.3 rollback protection the wrapper documents as a defense. Race window is small (microseconds) but the wrapper's purpose is to be robust against a misconfigured / hostile responder serving stale snapshots, and the race is reachable when the same hostile responder serves different chains to different concurrent validators.

Fix options: (a) introduce a put_crl_if_not_rollback(&self, key, candidate) trait method that lets the cache impl do an atomic compare-and-swap under its lock; (b) fold rollback into the cache impl itself (give the cache the policy); (c) hold a per-key lock around the get/put pair in the wrapper. (a) is least disruptive — extends the trait pre-1.0 once.
title: TOCTOU race in CachedHttpCrlFetcher::maybe_populate_cache rollback decision
